primary_claim: A steering direction extracted from an 'honest mechanic' vs 'car salesman' contrast in Gemma-2-2B-IT, when subtracted at layer ~10, reliably breaks hater/hype/toxic personas across multiple domains and snaps outputs toward literal, context-consistent reporting, whereas adding the same direction does not produce clean 'paltering' but instead induces high-arousal persuasive rhetoric and, at higher strengths, theatrical incoherence — a sign asymmetry not reproduced by a matched-norm random-vector control.
stated_future_work: Replicate the same protocol on a different instruct model
Replicate the same protocol on a larger model
Use a bigger, less template-driven contrast dataset for direction extraction
Localize the effect within layer 10 to specific heads/MLPs
Test steering the current token only, instead of all tokens
limitations_stated: Small dataset (n=5) and crude contrast used to extract the steering vector
Only one model tested (Gemma-2-2B-IT), so results could be model- or size-specific
Evaluation is qualitative (explicit rubric, but still eyeballing) with no quantified metrics reported
'Context fidelity' is defined narrowly as consistency with provided context, not real-world accuracy
The random-vector control used only one random vector, which is weak evidence against a generic 'any big vector' explanation
quote: subtracting this direction tends to snap outputs toward dry, ground-truth-consistent reporting
